clue.text: Raises swelling, discharge returning

parts.note: a bump is a small swelling

indicators.note: returning tells us the word for the discharge is read back to front

parts.note: pus is a discharge from a wound

explanation.surface: A patient reports a swelling whose discharge keeps coming back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returning' turns PUS into SUP, which follows BUMP.
explanation.definitionFit: To raise a price or level is to increase it, colloquially to push it higher.

clue.text: Onset of blind rage in clapped-out car

indicators.note: the onset of a word is its opening, so take just its first letter

parts.note: rage means anger

explanation.surface: A driver flies into a blind fury inside an old wreck of a car.
explanation.walkthrough: A BANGER is British slang for an old, worn-out car; 'in' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: British slang for a decrepit old vehicle, a sense the answer has alongside sausage.

clue.text: Amused swimming jellyfish

indicators.note: swimming suggests the letters move about and rearrange

explanation.surface: Someone is entertained watching jellyfish swim.
explanation.walkthrough: 'swimming' rearranges AMUSED.
explanation.definitionFit: The free-swimming bell-shaped stage of a jellyfish is called by this zoological name.

clue.text: Violin maker is avid art changed around beginning of Renaissance

indicators.note: around means the scrambled letters surround the next piece
changed means the letters of these words are rearranged
the beginning of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: An eager art lover's taste shifts around the start of the Renaissance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'changed' turns IS AVID ART into STRADIVAI, and 'around' puts it round R, the first letter of Renaissance.
explanation.definitionFit: Antonio Stradivari was the famous Italian craftsman whose stringed instruments are prized.

clue.text: Tread softly, concerned with army chaplain

parts.note: to pad is to walk quietly
re means about or concerning

explanation.surface: A chaplain moves quietly about his duties among soldiers.
explanation.definitionFit: A padre is the informal military name for a clergyman serving with the forces.

clue.text: More short stories containing no English people

indicators.note: short means the word loses its last letter

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: containing no means a letter is taken out of the word

parts.note: tales are stories

explanation.surface: A request for more brief tales without any English characters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'short' trims MORE to MOR; 'containing no' takes E out of TALES to leave TALS.
explanation.definitionFit: Mortals are human beings, as opposed to gods.

clue.text: Bloke perishes, split apart by extremely brutal jaws

parts.note: a bloke is a man

indicators.note: split apart by means the word is cut open with another piece put inside

parts.note: perishes means dies

indicators.note: extremely points to the extreme, first and last, letters of the word

explanation.surface: A man dies, torn apart by savage jaws.
explanation.walkthrough: 'extremely' gives BL, the first and last letters of brutal, which go inside DIES.
explanation.definitionFit: Mandibles are the lower jawbones, or the biting mouthparts of insects.

clue.text: Rubbish international bread

parts.note: rot means nonsense or rubbish

explanation.surface: Some foreign bread is dismissed as rubbish.
explanation.definitionFit: Roti is an unleavened flatbread from South Asia.

clue.text: Huge amount of water left over article in loft

indicators.note: in means these letters go inside the next word

parts.note: a loft is an attic

indicators.note: over in a down clue means the first piece sits above the second

parts.note: an is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A large leak of water has come down over something stored in the loft.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'over' puts L above AN; 'in' puts LAN inside ATTIC.
explanation.definitionFit: The Atlantic is the second-largest ocean on Earth.

clue.text: Primitive character interrupts wise man

indicators.note: interrupts means this piece breaks into the middle of the other

parts.note: a sage is a wise man
tone means character or quality

explanation.surface: A primitive figure cuts in while a wise man is talking.
explanation.definitionFit: The prehistoric era of stone tools gives an adjective for anything crude or outdated.

clue.text: Lowest part of drain broken

indicators.note: broken means the letters are smashed and rearranged

explanation.surface: The bottom of the drain has broken.
explanation.walkthrough: 'broken' rearranges DRAIN; 'of' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The nadir is the lowest point, the opposite of the zenith.

clue.text: £2 put in to give old Italian sculptor

parts.note: to put in money is to donate it
L stands for pound sterling, from Latin libra, so two pounds is two Ls

explanation.surface: Contributing two pounds earns you an old Italian sculpture.
explanation.walkthrough: The £ sign comes from L for libra, so '£2' is LL; 'to give' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Donatello was the Florentine Renaissance master of bronze and marble statues.

clue.text: Take your time to see Daisy performing

indicators.note: performing suggests the letters act out a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Relax and come along to watch Daisy on stage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'performing' rearranges TO SEE DAISY.
explanation.definitionFit: Both phrases are calming advice to go slowly and carefully.

clue.text: Formerly working with church

parts.note: on means working or functioning
CE stands for Church of England

explanation.surface: Someone used to work alongside the church.
explanation.definitionFit: The adverb means at one time in the past.

clue.text: Regularly stood between two labourers at close quarters

indicators.note: between means the picked letters are placed in the middle of the two words

parts.note: a hand is a manual worker, and there are two of them
the second of the two labourers, again a hand

indicators.note: regularly means take every other letter

explanation.surface: A man stood between two workers in a cramped space.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Regularly' takes TO from the alternate letters of stood, which goes between HAND and HAND.
explanation.definitionFit: Hand-to-hand fighting is combat at close range, body against body.

clue.text: Hesitant Midlands team keeping account can start to grow

indicators.note: keeping means the team holds the next piece inside it

parts.note: Aston Villa is a Birmingham football club, usually called Villa
a tin is a can

indicators.note: the start of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A dithering football club keeps the accountant while hoping to grow.
explanation.walkthrough: Aston Villa is a football club in Birmingham, in the English Midlands; 'keeping' puts AC inside VILLA.
explanation.definitionFit: Vacillating means wavering between choices, unable to decide.

clue.text: Duenna's tea with Evita ultimately polite

parts.note: cha is a slang word for tea
Eva Peron, known as Evita, was the wife of the Argentine president

indicators.note: ultimately means take the final letter

explanation.surface: A Spanish governess takes tea politely with Evita.
explanation.walkthrough: 's stands for 'is' as a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A duenna is an older woman who supervises girls in a Spanish family, so a protective escort.

clue.text: Pass on live question on 1970s PM, scratching head

parts.note: to be is to live or exist

indicators.note: scratching head means the first letter is removed

parts.note: Edward Heath was British Prime Minister from 1970 to 1974

explanation.surface: A Prime Minister of the seventies puzzles over a question, scratching his head.
explanation.walkthrough: Edward Heath was Britain's Prime Minister 1970-74; 'scratching head' removes his first letter H to leave EATH.
explanation.definitionFit: To bequeath is to leave property to someone in a will, handing it down.

clue.text: Plentiful cake scoffed by Adam Ant, but not in the morning

indicators.note: scoffed by means the cake is swallowed, going inside the other letters
but not means the following letters are removed

parts.note: AM means in the morning
a bun is a small cake

explanation.surface: Pop star Adam Ant eats a big cake, but never at breakfast time.
explanation.walkthrough: Adam Ant is a 1980s pop singer; removing AM from his name leaves ADANT, which 'scoffed by' wraps round BUN.
explanation.definitionFit: Abundant means present in large quantities.

clue.text: Make a mistake about business graduate and fool editor, ashamed

indicators.note: about means the first word goes around the next piece

parts.note: to err is to make a mistake
an MBA is a Master of Business Administration
an ass is a fool

explanation.surface: A business graduate and an editor err foolishly and feel shame.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts ERR round MBA, giving EMBARR.
explanation.definitionFit: To be embarrassed is to feel awkward and humiliated.

clue.text: Vast Russian region axing small European peninsula

indicators.note: axing means cutting a letter out

parts.note: Siberia is the huge region of northern Asian Russia

explanation.surface: A region of Russia is cut back to something small in Europe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'axing' removes S from SIBERIA.
explanation.definitionFit: Iberia is the peninsula shared by Spain and Portugal.

clue.text: After case cracked, Vice Squad finally stopped

indicators.note: cracked means the letters are broken up and rearranged
finally means take the last letter of each word

explanation.surface: Once a case is solved, the vice squad finally stands down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cracked' rearranges CASE to CEAS; 'finally' gives E and D, the last letters of Vice and Squad.
explanation.definitionFit: Ceased means halted or came to an end.

clue.text: Royal Navy intercepting US vessels

indicators.note: intercepting means the navy cuts into the middle of the other letters

explanation.surface: British warships stop American ships at sea.
explanation.definitionFit: Urns are vases or containers, and a vessel is any container.

clue.text: Folded bundle to be sorted out

indicators.note: sorted out suggests the letters are put into a new order

explanation.surface: A folded bundle waiting to be sorted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sorted out' rearranges BUNDLE TO BE.
explanation.definitionFit: Bent double means folded over at the waist, like something creased in half.

clue.text: Stunning form of apprehension?

parts.note: apprehension means arrest rather than worry, and a stunning arrest is one made with an electric stun gun

explanation.definitionFit: A Taser is an electric stun gun used by police to subdue a suspect being arrested.

clue.text: Desert island south of spit

indicators.note: south of in a down clue means the second piece goes below the first

parts.note: gob is slang for spit

explanation.surface: A desert island lies south of a spit of land.
explanation.walkthrough: GOB is British slang for spittle; in a down clue 'south of' puts I beneath it.
explanation.definitionFit: The Gobi is the great desert spanning Mongolia and northern China.

clue.text: Similar exotic lagoon in Australia

indicators.note: in means the rearranged letters go inside the other word
exotic suggests the letters take a strange new form

explanation.surface: A similar exotic lagoon can be found in Australia.
explanation.walkthrough: 'exotic' rearranges LAGOON to NALOGO, which 'in' places inside AUS.
explanation.definitionFit: Analogous means comparable or alike in some respect.

clue.text: Experts conserving river in large area of land

indicators.note: conserving means keeping the next piece safe inside

parts.note: aces are experts

explanation.surface: Experts protect a river running through a broad stretch of countryside.
explanation.definitionFit: Acres are units of land area, so many of them suggest a big estate.

clue.text: Direct link in hotel renewed

indicators.note: renewed means the letters are made over in a fresh arrangement

explanation.surface: A hotel installs a new direct phone line.
explanation.walkthrough: 'renewed' rearranges IN HOTEL.
explanation.definitionFit: A hotline is a dedicated phone line for immediate contact, as between heads of state.

clue.text: Indication to leave eg Queen of Diamonds

explanation.definitionFit: A football referee shows a red card to send a player off; any heart or diamond card is a red playing card.
